learning_target: Useful focus now

learning_target: Three moments and their triggers
correct_concept: Describe at least three moments, their information needs and what triggers each shift.
feedback: Worked example: Open play: scan teammates. Whistle: listen to the official. Free throw: find the chosen rim target. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Cue examples and selection
correct_concept: Give one instructional and one motivational cue. Select one for the case and explain why.
feedback: Worked example: “See the target” directs attention; “commit” supports effort. Jordan first needs the target cue. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Anchor and use
correct_concept: Name a return point, when it is used and the next action.
feedback: Worked example: At the line, the rim target is the anchor. Jordan finds it before following the familiar setup. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Before-performance sequence
correct_concept: Write a labelled sequence. Explain what each part directs attention toward.
feedback: Worked example: Prepare: check the starting position. Direct: find the target and use “smooth.” Begin: take the practised shot. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Disruption and response
correct_concept: Name the signal, response and next task cue. Include clarification when instructions are missing.
feedback: Worked example: If the drill order changes and the role is unclear, ask where to begin, then identify the next cue. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Walkthrough with a changed demand
correct_concept: Describe one appropriate variation, what stays the same and what the performer would observe.
feedback: Worked example: In a hypothetical practice, shorten the preparation pause. Keep the task the same and check whether the essential target cue is still used. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Observation and adjustment
correct_concept: Describe a factual observation and one adjustment it could support. Label invented observations as hypothetical.
feedback: Worked example: Hypothetically, Jordan looks away before the signal. Review the trigger for returning to the target rather than label Jordan as unfocused. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Adapt to an unfamiliar task
correct_concept: New case: a musician is moved from a solo to a duet. Explain a changed focus, a useful cue and a disruption response.
feedback: Worked example: The duet adds a partner’s timing cue. Plan a shared entry and return point rather than using the solo routine unchanged. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.

learning_target: Why attention must change

feedback: Worked example: The passing decision needs several external cues, while a free throw uses a precise target. One missed cue does not identify every possible cause. Evaluate with the four-dimension rubric; other supported responses can be valid.
